{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PDMWJbAZfccUuU7wfBd6bT","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Run onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#94\n4\tLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n5\t\n6\t## Why\n7\t\n8\t`beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.\n9\t\n10\tThat breaks the guarantee the hook names imply. A deployer who allocates something in `beforeSession` — a span, a database handle, a rate-limit token — and releases it in `afterSession` leaks it on exactly the path where the allocation failed, and learns nothing from `onError` because it never fires. The failure is silent in the engine and visible only as an unexplained rejection at the caller.\n11\t\n12\tRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n13\t\n14\t## What to do\n15\t\n16\tMove the `beforeSession` call inside the `try`, so a throw from it reaches the same `catch` and `finally` as any other failure in the turn, and decide one question explicitly: whether `afterSession` running after a failed `beforeSession` is what a deployer wants, or whether it needs to know the session never started. Record the answer in the spec either way, because a cleanup hook that cannot tell \"never allocated\" from \"allocated and finished\" is a new trap for the same reader.\n17\t\n18\t## Acceptance criteria\n19\t\n20\t- [ ] A `beforeSession` that throws still reaches the caller as a rejection, unchanged from today\n21\t- [ ] `onError` fires for that throw, with the same argument shape as any other orchestrator failure\n22\t- [ ] `afterSession` fires for that throw, and the spec states what a hook can assume about how much of the turn happened\n23\t- [ ] A non-throwing `beforeSession` behaves exactly as today, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n24\t- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n25\t- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n26\t\n27\t## Tech notes\n28\t\n29\tKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `beforeSession` call above the `try`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n30\t\n31\tOut of scope: the `instanceof Error` gate on `onError` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n32\t\n33\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"77442a80-7837-42de-ad22-f424c1cf24c4","uuid":"92fd0134-0e76-41ab-afe5-b96c1f058d4d","timestamp":"2026-11-06T22:17:33.018Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/47e628fdc437/workspace/ticket.md","content":"# Run onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws\n\nIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#94\nLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n\n## Why\n\n`beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.\n\nThat breaks the guarantee the hook names imply. A deployer who allocates something in `beforeSession` — a span, a database handle, a rate-limit token — and releases it in `afterSession` leaks it on exactly the path where the allocation failed, and learns nothing from `onError` because it never fires. The failure is silent in the engine and visible only as an unexplained rejection at the caller.\n\nRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n\n## What to do\n\nMove the `beforeSession` call inside the `try`, so a throw from it reaches the same `catch` and `finally` as any other failure in the turn, and decide one question explicitly: whether `afterSession` running after a failed `beforeSession` is what a deployer wants, or whether it needs to know the session never started. Record the answer in the spec either way, because a cleanup hook that cannot tell \"never allocated\" from \"allocated and finished\" is a new trap for the same reader.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A `beforeSession` that throws still reaches the caller as a rejection, unchanged from today\n- [ ] `onError` fires for that throw, with the same argument shape as any other orchestrator failure\n- [ ] `afterSession` fires for that throw, and the spec states what a hook can assume about how much of the turn happened\n- [ ] A non-throwing `beforeSession` behaves exactly as today, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n\n## Tech notes\n\nKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `beforeSession` call above the `try`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: the `instanceof Error` gate on `onError` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n\n","numLines":33,"startLine":1,"totalLines":33}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01PDMWJbAZfccUuU7wfBd6bT","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

 if (clientMessages.length > 0) {\n            yield {type: 'tool_result' as const, clientMessages};\n          }\n\n          if (suppressOutput) {\n            yield {type: 'suppress_output' as const};\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (hooks?.afterModelResponse) await hooks.afterModelResponse(session, responseText, lastUsage);\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (hooks?.onError && error instanceof Error) {\n          await hooks.onError(session, error);\n        }\n        throw error;\n      } finally {\n        // Before both: a provider that threw mid-stream leaves an entry open, and nothing should persist it that way.\n        commitStreamingEntries(session);\n        try {\n          if (hooks?.afterSession) await hooks.afterSession(session);\n        } finally {\n          await saveSession(sessionStore, session);\n        }\n      }\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// A negative budget means no tool rounds; a non-finite one, NaN included, falls back to the default rather than never ending.\nfunction normalizeToolRounds(value: number | undefined): number {\n  if (value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS;\n  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));\n}\n\n// Gates execution, not the provider call: a round nobody can read is never run, and the call that read the last one already has.\nfunction budgetSpent(round: number, maxToolRounds: number, pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): boolean {\n  if (round < maxToolRounds) return false;\n  log.warn('orchestrator', 'tool budget exhausted', {\n    maxToolRounds,\n    requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name),\n  });\n  return true;\n}\n\n// The stop always follows the text: the round's own stop already committed its entry, and a bare text chunk would open one never committed.\nasync function* closeExhaustedTurn(\n  session: ChatSession,\n  budget: ToolBudgetInfo,\n  hook?: OnToolBudgetExhausted\n): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, string> {\n  const sentence = (hook ? await hook(session, budget) : undefined) ?? '';\n  if (sentence !== '') yield {type: 'text', text: sentence};\n  yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED};\n  return sentence;\n}\n\ninterface RoundOutcome {\n  stopReason: string;\n  text: string;\n  usage?: UsageMetadata;\n}\n\n// `yield*` in the caller evaluates to this return, so the round's totals come back as data.\nasync function* streamRound(\n  provider: AIProvider,\n  request: SendMessageParams,\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]\n): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, RoundOutcome> {\n  let stopReason = '';\n  let text = '';\n  let usage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n\n  for await (const chunk of provider.sendMessage(request)) {\n    yield chunk;\n    collectToolCalls(chunk, pendingToolCalls);\n    stopReason = extractStopReason(chunk) ?? stopReason;\n    usage = extractUsage(chunk) ?? usage;\n    if (chunk.type === 'text') text += chunk.text;\n  }\n\n  return {stopReason, text, usage};\n}\n\n// A changed message is also written back to the session's last user entry.\nasync function rewriteUserMessage(\n  session: ChatSession,\n  userMessage: string,\n  hook: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<string>\n): Promise<string> {\n  const modified = await hook(session, userMessage);\n  if (modified === userMessage) return userMessage;\n\n  updateLastUserContent(session, modified);\n  return modified;\n}\n\nfunction lastUserContent(session: ChatSession): string {\n  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const entry = session.entries[i];\n    if (entry.role === 'user') return entry.content;\n  }\n  return '';\n}\n\nfunction updateLastUserContent(session: ChatSession, content: string): void {\n  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const entry = session.entries[i];\n    if (entry.role === 'user') {\n      entry.content = content;\n      return;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// One runner per round: the policy sees each known call before its executor, and an unknown name keeps the registry's own path.\nfunction toolCallRunner(toolRegistry: ToolRegistry, session: ChatSession, beforeToolCall?: BeforeToolCall) {\n  const context: ToolContext = {\n    userId: session.userId,\n    sessionId: session.sessionId,\n    workspaceId: session.workspaceId,\n    authHeaders: session.authHeaders,\n  };\n\n  return async (tc: ToolCall): Promise<ToolResponse> => {\n    const declined =\n      beforeToolCall && toolRegistry.has(tc.name) ? await consultPolicy(beforeToolCall, session, tc) : undefined;\n    return declined ?? toolRegistry.execute(tc.name, tc.input, context);\n  };\n}\n\n// A throwing policy declines its call rather than failing the turn: every tool_use must still be answered.\nasync function consultPolicy(\n  policy: BeforeToolCall,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  tc: ToolCall\n): Promise<ToolResponse | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await policy(session, tc);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.warn('orchestrator', 'beforeToolCall threw, so the call is declined', {\n      tool: tc.name,\n      errorType: error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error,\n    });\n    return {result: `The ${tc.name} call was declined and not performed.`};\n  }\n}\n\nasync function executeToolCalls(\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[],\n  messages: Message[],\n  session: ChatSession,\n  runToolCall: (tc: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse>\n): Promise<ToolExecutionResult> {\n  messages.push(buildToolCallMessages(pendingToolCalls));\n\n  const responses = await Promise.all(\n    pendingToolCalls.map(async tc => {\n      const response = await runToolCall(tc);\n      return {tc, response};\n    })\n  );\n\n  const toolResults: ToolResultContent[] = responses.map(({tc, response}) => ({\n    type: 'tool_result' as const,\n    toolUseId: tc.id,\n    content: response.result,\n  }));\n  messages.push({role: 'user', content: toolResults});\n\n  const rawClientMessages = responses.flatMap(({response}) => response.clientMessages ?? []);\n\n  return {\n    clientMessages: assignEntryIndices(rawClientMessages, session),\n    suppressOutput: responses.some(({response}) => response.suppressAssistantResponse === true),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction assignEntryIndices(clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[], session: ChatSession): OutgoingMessage[] {\n  return clientMessages.map(msg => {\n    if (msg.type !== 'entry_upsert') return msg;\n    const index = appendEntry(session, msg.entry);\n    return {...msg, index};\n  });\n}\n\n// A store outage is not a reason to fail the turn the customer already received.\nasync function saveSession(store: SessionStore | undefined, session: ChatSession): Promise<void> {\n  if (!store?.save) return;\n\n  try {\n    await store.save(session);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    log.error('orchestrator', 'session save failed', {sessionId: session.sessionId, error: message});\n  }\n}\n","numLines":335,"startLine":1,"totalLines":335}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01XmYbUKQwXzywPD6AycdcM8","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MKr3xgYFo5fCJdxztiG9Hk","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n2\t\n3\t| Field  | Value                |\n4\t| ------ | -------------------- |\n5\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n6\t| Status | Shipped              |\n7\t\n8\t`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n9\t\n10\t## Installing hooks through config\n11\t\n12\t- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n13\t- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n14\t- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n15\t- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L194)).\n16\t- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n17\t\n18\t## Engine startup\n19\t\n20\t- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n21\t\n22\t## Measured semantics — out of scope\n23\t\n24\tThese three properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` are recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue changes none of them; each is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.\n25\t\n26\t- `beforeSession` is inside the `try` block, so a throw there reaches the `catch`/`finally` blocks, firing both `onError` and `afterSession`, where a deployer can assume no tools were run and the turn was aborted before provider interaction ([validated by: runs onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.beforeSession.acceptance.test.ts#L40)).\n27\t- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n28\t- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L148](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L148)), and is passed the `lastUsage` local — the most recent round's usage, not a sum across tool rounds, so a deployer using the hook for billing or audit under-counts every turn that ran tools.\n29\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"77442a80-7837-42de-ad22-f424c1cf24c4","uuid":"37fa3978-2bee-42f3-9057-1bc33fdc3ade","timestamp":"2026-11-06T22:18:48.270Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/47e628fdc437/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md","content":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L194)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n\n## Measured semantics — out of scope\n\nThese three properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` are recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue changes none of them; each is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.\n\n- `beforeSession` is inside the `try` block, so a throw there reaches the `catch`/`finally` blocks, firing both `onError` and `afterSession`, where a deployer can assume no tools were run and the turn was aborted before provider interaction ([validated by: runs onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.beforeSession.acceptance.test.ts#L40)).\n- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L148](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L148)), and is passed the `lastUsage` local — the most recent round's usage, not a sum across tool rounds, so a deployer using the hook for billing or audit under-counts every turn that ran tools.\n","numLines":29,"startLine":1,"totalLines":29}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01MKr3xgYFo5fCJdxztiG9Hk","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HRfxW5gQEr4LLZ3M9ow6mC","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Changelog\n2\t\n3\tAll notable changes to `@re-cinq/hal-engine` are documented here.\n4\t\n5\tThe format is [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to\n6\t[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Entries are written for somebody installing the\n7\tpackage, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.\n8\t\n9\t## [Unreleased]\n10\t\n11\t### Added\n12\t\n13\t- `SessionStore` gains an optional `save(session)` member: the write signal a durable store needs. The engine calls it once per processed user message, from the same `finally` path that runs `afterSession`, so it fires for a turn that ended in a provider error as well as one that succeeded — a store that only heard about successes would lose exactly the conversations a customer complains about. By the time it runs, the turn's entries are committed, so the assistant entry's `isStreaming` is already `false` — including when a provider threw mid-stream, where the engine now closes the open entry before saving, recording `truncated` on it, rather than persisting a half-streamed entry that looks finished. An `afterSession` hook that throws no longer costs the turn its write signal. What `save` throws or rejects with is caught and logged as one line carrying the session id, and the turn continues: the client still receives its full stream and `stream_end`, because a database outage is not a reason for the agent to stop answering. The member is typed `void | Promise<void>`, so a synchronous implementation and an `async` one both satisfy it. Additive: `InMemorySessionStore` does not implement `save` and is unchanged, and a store that omits it behaves exactly as before.\n14\t- `SessionStore` gains an optional `evict(sessionId)` member, and `InMemorySessionStore` implements it. The engine calls it only for a session whose socket closed while `create` was still pending — one that no client ever received and that has no entries to keep. `InMemorySessionStore` now also takes `{maxAgeMs}` (default `28_800_000`, eight hours), exported as `InMemorySessionStoreOptions`. Expired sessions are evicted when read and swept at the head of `create`, which stops at the first live session, so the bound costs nothing on a busy store. There is no timer: a library-owned interval would keep your process alive.\n15\t- **`MongoSessionStore`**, a durable session store, exported as `MongoSessionStore` and `createMongoSessionStore`. It takes a collection, a client with a database name, or a connection URL — nothing in the package reads the environment or assumes a host. The collection is the truth and the in-process cache is an optimisation: a session written by `save` is readable by a second store on the same collection. `delete` removes the document — it is the consumer's erasure primitive and the engine never calls it — as do `eraseConversation`, `eraseOlderThan(cutoff)` and `eraseAll`, while `clear` alone touches only the cache; `docs/session-stores.md` opens with the table that says which is which, because the previous documentation would have led you to believe `delete` erased. Documents carry `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, so a retention period is expressible without per-entry timestamps. **No credential is ever written**: `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` and `host` are stripped at any depth, not just the top level, and the same `stripCredentialKeys` is exported for stores you write yourself. `mongodb` is an optional peer dependency loaded only when the store actually connects, so a consumer who installs no optional peer can still import the package root and use the in-memory store. **Migration note**: `delete` and `evict` both erase on this store, so the one-line `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` that restores the pre-0.4 close behaviour destroys the conversation on every socket close — point `onDisconnect` at neither. Nothing needs reclaiming by hand: the in-process cache is bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours by default) and drops stale entries without touching a document. This does **not** deliver conversation resume, and it does not make the engine safe to run as more than one instance against one conversation.\n16\t\n17\t### Changed\n18\t\n19\t- Every `SessionStore` member is now `Awaitable<T>` (`T | Promise<T>`) rather than a bare `T`, so a store backed by a database is expressible for the first time. `Awaitable` is exported from the package root. **A synchronous implementation needs no change** — `T` is assignable to `T | Promise<T>` in a return position — and `InMemorySessionStore` is unedited. The WebSocket connection handler now awaits `create` and the release that follows a close: it pauses the socket across the await so a frame sent before `connected` arrives is buffered rather than dropped, attaches its `close` listener before the await so a socket that closes mid-create leaves no session behind, and catches a rejection from either call so one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process with an unhandled rejection. **Migration note**: the `connected` frame now arrives one tick later, after the awaited `create`, so a client that waits for it (as the protocol already requires) sees no difference; only code that assumed the frame was emitted synchronously with the upgrade does.\n20\t- **The engine no longer erases a conversation when its socket closes.** The WebSocket close handler called `sessionStore.delete(sessionId)` unconditionally, which meant that behind a durable store every conversation was written and then destroyed the moment the customer closed their tab — the opposite of what this engine's own documentation promised. `SessionStore.delete` now has no engine-internal caller at all and is purely your erasure primitive. The credentials the socket carried are cleared from the session on close, since they were issued for a request that is over; the entries are untouched. **Migration note**: to restore the old behaviour exactly, pass `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` — that one line is the whole migration. If you rely on the default store not growing, note that it is now bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours) rather than by the close handler; that is a memory bound, not a retention policy, and the retention decision remains yours.\n21\t\n22\t## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-29\n23\t\n24\t**Upgrading from 0.2.x.** Nothing is removed and no existing signature changes, but check these before you bump:\n25\t\n26\t- `OrchestratorHooks` gains two optional members, `beforeToolCall` and `onToolBudgetExhausted`. Code that checks the hooks exhaustively, for example `satisfies Record<keyof OrchestratorHooks, …>`, fails to type-check until it names both.\n27\t- `ToolRegistry.execute` now validates tool input against each tool's `inputSchema`, so a tool that produced its own message for malformed input receives only valid input; the model reads the registry's validation message instead.\n28\t- `maxToolRounds` now counts executed rounds: the default of 5 runs 5 tool rounds, not 6. Raise it by one to keep the old count.\n29\t- Offering a bare access token as the only WebSocket subprotocol still works but is deprecated: offer `hal.v1` beside it now, because the next minor release stops accepting a bare token.\n30\t- New dependencies: `ajv`, and `cookie` moves from `^0.7` to `^2`.\n31\t\n32\t### Added\n33\t\n34\t- `VertexConfig` gains an optional `apiEndpoint` field, forwarded verbatim to the `@google-cloud/vertexai` SDK constructor. Deployers who must keep inference in the EU multi-region can set `apiEndpoint: 'aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com'`; the change is additive and the default behaviour (endpoint derived from `location`) is unchanged.\n35\t- `HalEngineConfig.transport` now accepts three optional extension points: `additionalRoutes` (mounts a router under `basePath`, unauthenticated), `rootRoutes` (mounts a router at `/`, after the `basePath` router and before the 404 catch-all), and `errorHandler` (replaces Express's default HTML error page). Pass none of them and the app is identical to before. See `docs/getting-started.md` for usage and the GDPR / NIS-2 notes that apply to unauthenticated routes.\n36\t- `OrchestratorHooks` gains an optional `beforeToolCall(session, call)` hook that fires before each known tool's executor, once per call per round. Return `undefined` to let the call run, or a `ToolResponse` to decline it: the executor is skipped and the model reads your `result` as that call's `tool_result`, with `clientMessages` and `suppressAssistantResponse` behaving as a tool's would. A hook that throws declines the call instead of failing the turn. Use it for an audit of what the model attempted or an EU AI Act Article 14 human-oversight control. The hook receives the model's raw tool input and, through `session`, the caller's `authHeaders`, so don't log either. Additive: with no hook installed, nothing changes.\n37\t- `OrchestratorHooks` gains an optional `onToolBudgetExhausted(session, budget)` hook, and `ToolBudgetInfo` (`{maxToolRounds, requestedTools}`) and `TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` are exported. It fires when the model asks for a tool round `maxToolRounds` refuses, after the last provider call and before `afterModelResponse`. Return a sentence and the turn ends on it as an ordinary assistant entry, so the user sees a degraded answer instead of silence; the engine writes no prose of its own. Every exhausted run now also ends with a `{type: 'stop', stopReason: 'tool_budget_exhausted'}` chunk, a new value for the existing field rather than a new type, which the WebSocket transport sends nothing for. The turn still ends with `stream_end`, never `error`. Additive: with no hook installed, the wire is unchanged.\n38\t- `AssistantEntry` and `ThinkingEntry` gain an optional `truncated: true`, set on an entry the run could not finish: a provider failure mid-stream, or a round that ends on a tool call with no `stop`. The server re-sends such an entry as an `entry_upsert` carrying the flag just before its `entry_commit`, and the flag stays on the stored entry, so a client can render a cut-off answer as cut off live or on a replay, without relying on the transient `error` frame. An entry committed normally never carries it; a suppressed entry is flagged in the session but never re-sent. Text the thinking-tag parser was still holding back is now kept in a cut-off entry, as it already was on a normal stop. Additive: a client that ignores the field renders what it did before, and the extra `entry_upsert` replaces the entry with the content it already has.\n39\t\n40\t### Changed\n41\t\n42\t- Every `user_message` now ends in exactly one `stream_end`, including a run that fails and a message that fails validation; the `error` frame is advisory rather than terminal. Entries are written for somebody installing the\npackage, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- `SessionStore` gains an optional `save(session)` member: the write signal a durable store needs. The engine calls it once per processed user message, from the same `finally` path that runs `afterSession`, so it fires for a turn that ended in a provider error as well as one that succeeded — a store that only heard about successes would lose exactly the conversations a customer complains about. By the time it runs, the turn's entries are committed, so the assistant entry's `isStreaming` is already `false` — including when a provider threw mid-stream, where the engine now closes the open entry before saving, recording `truncated` on it, rather than persisting a half-streamed entry that looks finished. An `afterSession` hook that throws no longer costs the turn its write signal. What `save` throws or rejects with is caught and logged as one line carrying the session id, and the turn continues: the client still receives its full stream and `stream_end`, because a database outage is not a reason for the agent to stop answering. The member is typed `void | Promise<void>`, so a synchronous implementation and an `async` one both satisfy it. Additive: `InMemorySessionStore` does not implement `save` and is unchanged, and a store that omits it behaves exactly as before.\n- `SessionStore` gains an optional `evict(sessionId)` member, and `InMemorySessionStore` implements it. The engine calls it only for a session whose socket closed while `create` was still pending — one that no client ever received and that has no entries to keep. `InMemorySessionStore` now also takes `{maxAgeMs}` (default `28_800_000`, eight hours), exported as `InMemorySessionStoreOptions`. Expired sessions are evicted when read and swept at the head of `create`, which stops at the first live session, so the bound costs nothing on a busy store. There is no timer: a library-owned interval would keep your process alive.\n- **`MongoSessionStore`**, a durable session store, exported as `MongoSessionStore` and `createMongoSessionStore`. It takes a collection, a client with a database name, or a connection URL — nothing in the package reads the environment or assumes a host. The collection is the truth and the in-process cache is an optimisation: a session written by `save` is readable by a second store on the same collection. `delete` removes the document — it is the consumer's erasure primitive and the engine never calls it — as do `eraseConversation`, `eraseOlderThan(cutoff)` and `eraseAll`, while `clear` alone touches only the cache; `docs/session-stores.md` opens with the table that says which is which, because the previous documentation would have led you to believe `delete` erased. Documents carry `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, so a retention period is expressible without per-entry timestamps. **No credential is ever written**: `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` and `host` are stripped at any depth, not just the top level, and the same `stripCredentialKeys` is exported for stores you write yourself. `mongodb` is an optional peer dependency loaded only when the store actually connects, so a consumer who installs no optional peer can still import the package root and use the in-memory store. **Migration note**: `delete` and `evict` both erase on this store, so the one-line `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` that restores the pre-0.4 close behaviour destroys the conversation on every socket close — point `onDisconnect` at neither. Nothing needs reclaiming by hand: the in-process cache is bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours by default) and drops stale entries without touching a document. This does **not** deliver conversation resume, and it does not make the engine safe to run as more than one instance against one conversation.\n\n### Changed\n\n- Every `SessionStore` member is now `Awaitable<T>` (`T | Promise<T>`) rather than a bare `T`, so a store backed by a database is expressible for the first time. `Awaitable` is exported from the package root. **A synchronous implementation needs no change** — `T` is assignable to `T | Promise<T>` in a return position — and `InMemorySessionStore` is unedited. The WebSocket connection handler now awaits `create` and the release that follows a close: it pauses the socket across the await so a frame sent before `connected` arrives is buffered rather than dropped, attaches its `close` listener before the await so a socket that closes mid-create leaves no session behind, and catches a rejection from either call so one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process with an unhandled rejection. **Migration note**: the `connected` frame now arrives one tick later, after the awaited `create`, so a client that waits for it (as the protocol already requires) sees no difference; only code that assumed the frame was emitted synchronously with the upgrade does.\n- **The engine no longer erases a conversation when its socket closes.** The WebSocket close handler called `sessionStore.delete(sessionId)` unconditionally, which meant that behind a durable store every conversation was written and then destroyed the moment the customer closed their tab — the opposite of what this engine's own documentation promised. `SessionStore.delete` now has no engine-internal caller at all and is purely your erasure primitive. The credentials the socket carried are cleared from the session on close, since they were issued for a request that is over; the entries are untouched. **Migration note**: to restore the old behaviour exactly, pass `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` — that one line is the whole migration. If you rely on the default store not growing, note that it is now bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours) rather than by the close handler; that is a memory bound, not a retention policy, and the retention decision remains yours.\n\n## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-29\n\n**Upgrading from 0.2.x.** Nothing is removed and no existing signature changes, but check these before you bump:\n\n- `OrchestratorHooks` gains two optional members, `beforeToolCall` and `onToolBudgetExhausted`. Code that checks the hooks exhaustively, for example `satisfies Record<keyof OrchestratorHooks, …>`, fails to type-check until it names both.\n- `ToolRegistry.execute` now validates tool input against each tool's `inputSchema`, so a tool that produced its own message for malformed input receives only valid input; the model reads the registry's validation message instead.\n- `maxToolRounds` now counts executed rounds: the default of 5 runs 5 tool rounds, not 6. Raise it by one to keep the old count.\n- Offering a bare access token as the only WebSocket subprotocol still works but is deprecated: offer `hal.v1` beside it now, because the next minor release stops accepting a bare token.\n- New dependencies: `ajv`, and `cookie` moves from `^0.7` to `^2`.\n\n### Added\n\n- `VertexConfig` gains an optional `apiEndpoint` field, forwarded verbatim to the `@google-cloud/vertexai` SDK constructor. Deployers who must keep inference in the EU multi-region can set `apiEndpoint: 'aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com'`; the change is additive and the default behaviour (endpoint derived from `location`) is unchanged.\n- `HalEngineConfig.transport` now accepts three optional extension points: `additionalRoutes` (mounts a router under `basePath`, unauthenticated), `rootRoutes` (mounts a router at `/`, after the `basePath` router and before the 404 catch-all), and `errorHandler` (replaces Express's default HTML error page). Pass none of them and the app is identical to before. See `docs/getting-started.md` for usage and the GDPR / NIS-2 notes that apply to unauthenticated routes.\n- `OrchestratorHooks` gains an optional `beforeToolCall(session, call)` hook that fires before each known tool's executor, once per call per round. Return `undefined` to let the call run, or a `ToolResponse` to decline it: the executor is skipped and the model reads your `result` as that call's `tool_result`, with `clientMessages` and `suppressAssistantResponse` behaving as a tool's would. A hook that throws declines the call instead of failing the turn. Use it for an audit of what the model attempted or an EU AI Act Article 14 human-oversight control. The hook receives the model's raw tool input and, through `session`, the caller's `authHeaders`, so don't log either. Additive: with no hook installed, nothing changes.\n- `OrchestratorHooks` gains an optional `onToolBudgetExhausted(session, budget)` hook, and `ToolBudgetInfo` (`{maxToolRounds, requestedTools}`) and `TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` are exported. It fires when the model asks for a tool round `maxToolRounds` refuses, after the last provider call and before `afterModelResponse`. Return a sentence and the turn ends on it as an ordinary assistant entry, so the user sees a degraded answer instead of silence; the engine writes no prose of its own. Every exhausted run now also ends with a `{type: 'stop', stopReason: 'tool_budget_exhausted'}` chunk, a new value for the existing field rather than a new type, which the WebSocket transport sends nothing for. The turn still ends with `stream_end`, never `error`. Additive: with no hook installed, the wire is unchanged.\n- `AssistantEntry` and `ThinkingEntry` gain an optional `truncated: true`, set on an entry the run could not finish: a provider failure mid-stream, or a round that ends on a tool call with no `stop`.
